title: How to Prove a Gut Synapse

scenes.tts: A cell in the gut lining is not a neuron. How could it send a rapid message to a vagal sensory neuron?
scenes.visual: HOOK AND CARRIED WORLD, 16:9. COLOUR MAP FOR BOTH CHAPTERS: enteroendocrine sensor cell GOLD; vagal neuron BLUE; glutamate TEAL; diffuse hormone route GREY; unidentified items WHITE; active or restored result GREEN; blocked or silenced result RED. Show a cross-section filling 70% of frame height: gut lumen above, epithelial sheet across the middle, tissue below. One GOLD sensor cell grows a narrow basal process toward a thick BLUE vagal axon. A question mark pulses in the remaining gap. Nutrient dots drift in the lumen and the axon gently undulates. Large question at top: 'How does this cell reach the nerve?'
scenes.narration: A cell in the gut lining is not a neuron. How could it send a rapid message to a vagal sensory neuron?

scenes.visual: Title 'How to Prove a Gut Synapse' writes across the lumen while nutrient dots continue drifting. The title clears, leaving the same gut cross-section and colour map.

scenes.tts: One possibility is a hormone released into nearby tissue. Another is a point-to-point synapse. Speed alone will not settle the choice.
scenes.visual: The GOLD cell releases GREY dots that diffuse broadly through tissue toward several faint targets. Beside that route, its basal process completes a precise contact with the BLUE axon; a WHITE unidentified-messenger dot waits at the contact. Label both routes 'schematic'. A clock appears, then splits so neither route receives a winning check mark.
scenes.narration: One possibility is a hormone released into nearby tissue. Another is a point-to-point synapse. Speed alone will not settle the choice.

scenes.tts: Start with anatomy. Modified rabies virus begins in selected enteroendocrine cells and labels connected nerves. In some mice, labelling reaches vagal nodose neurons.
scenes.visual: Keep the gut world. Small WHITE tracer sparks begin inside the GOLD cell, move down its process and illuminate the BLUE axon toward a simple nodose-ganglion oval at frame right. A counter card reads 'some mice'. The contact glows, but the WHITE unidentified-messenger dot remains a question mark.
scenes.narration: Start with anatomy. Modified rabies virus begins in selected enteroendocrine cells and labels connected nerves. In some mice, labelling reaches vagal nodose neurons.

scenes.tts: Tracing can map a connection across the epithelial boundary. It cannot show rapid transmission, identify the messenger, or reveal whether the connection changes nerve firing. The picture must become physiology.
scenes.visual: The tracer-lit gut contact stays large at left. Three unanswered cards stack at right: 'how fast?', 'which messenger?', and 'changes firing?'. The tracing sparks fade into a thin anatomical outline while an empty current plot expands to fill the right half.
scenes.narration: Tracing can map a connection across the epithelial boundary. It cannot show rapid transmission, identify the messenger, or reveal whether the connection changes nerve firing. The picture must become physiology.

scenes.tts: That establishes connectivity, not the transmitter. The cells also carry transcripts for vesicular glutamate transporter one. Those transcripts fit glutamate release, but still do not show a current.
scenes.caption: That establishes connectivity, not the transmitter. The cells also carry transcripts for VGLUT1. Those transcripts fit glutamate release, but still do not show a current.
scenes.visual: The illuminated connection compresses into a card labelled 'connected'. A separate TEAL label 'VGLUT1 transcript' appears inside the GOLD cell. Both cards slide beneath an empty current plot whose flat baseline continues moving. A large 'not yet' sits beside the trace.
scenes.narration: That establishes connectivity, not the transmitter. The cells also carry transcripts for VGLUT1. Those transcripts fit glutamate release, but still do not show a current.

scenes.tts: Now move the cell and a nodose neuron into a dish. Light activates the gut cell. Within sixty to eight hundred milliseconds, an excitatory current appears in the neuron.
scenes.caption: Now move the cell and a nodose neuron into a dish. Light activates the gut cell. Within 60 to 800 milliseconds, an excitatory current appears in the neuron.
scenes.visual: The GOLD cell and BLUE axon lift from the gut into a large culture dish without changing positions. A GREEN light pulse hits the GOLD cell; WHITE unidentified-messenger dots cross the contact. A current plot labelled 'schematic trace' grows a downward deflection. A computed linear time bar spans 60 to 800 ms and is labelled 'measured range'.
scenes.narration: Now move the cell and a nodose neuron into a dish. Light activates the gut cell. Within 60 to 800 milliseconds, an excitatory current appears in the neuron.

scenes.tts: That current measures the neuron's response directly. Its sub-second latency supports a fast messenger in this dish. But one current still cannot establish which receptors carry it.
scenes.visual: The current trace enlarges and receives a GREEN badge 'direct neuronal response'. The dish boundary remains visible around it. A WHITE unidentified-messenger dot approaches three differently shaped, unlabelled receptor blocks on the BLUE neuron; question marks appear above all three.
scenes.narration: That current measures the neuron's response directly. Its sub-second latency supports a fast messenger in this dish. But one current still cannot establish which receptors carry it.

scenes.tts: Kynurenic acid blocks ionotropic glutamate receptors, and the current disappears. If receptors are blocked rather than cells damaged, what should happen after washout?
scenes.visual: A RED blocker bar covers receptors on the BLUE neuron. TEAL dots reach the bar and stop; the moving trace becomes flat. The question fills the upper half: 'Blocked receptors or damaged cells?' A small wash bottle waits at lower right.
scenes.narration: Kynurenic acid blocks ionotropic glutamate receptors, and the current disappears. If receptors are blocked rather than cells damaged, what should happen after washout?

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Keep the question on screen. The blocker bar pulses faintly, the flat trace crawls forward and fluid in the dish shimmers; no answer appears.

scenes.tts: Washout removes the blocker, and the current returns. Recovery supports receptor block rather than cell damage. Together, latency and reversible pharmacology identify fast glutamate action on the neuron.
scenes.visual: Fluid sweeps the RED blocker away. Receptors return BLUE; TEAL dots cross again and the current deflection grows back GREEN. The question transforms into two linked badges: 'fast current' and 'reversible glutamate block'.
scenes.narration: Washout removes the blocker, and the current returns. Recovery supports receptor block rather than cell damage. Together, latency and reversible pharmacology identify fast glutamate action on the neuron.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. No single result proves the route. A fast synapse is established when anatomy, timing, pharmacology and causal perturbation converge.
scenes.visual: Return the cell-neuron pair to the gut cross-section. Four large segments close into one chain around the contact: 'anatomy', 'timing', 'pharmacology', 'causality'. Each segment arrives as named and locks to the next. The synaptic contact glows TEAL only when the chain closes.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. No single result proves the route. A fast synapse is established when anatomy, timing, pharmacology and causal perturbation converge.

scenes.tts: Causality comes from the living mouse. Intestinal sucrose raises cervical-vagus firing. Blocking sodium glucose transporter one removes that response, placing the sugar sensor upstream.
scenes.caption: Causality comes from the living mouse. Intestinal sucrose raises cervical-vagus firing. Blocking SGLT1 removes that response, placing the sugar sensor upstream.
scenes.visual: Nutrient dots in the lumen turn GOLD and enter the GOLD cell through a labelled block 'SGLT1'. A live firing raster beside the BLUE axon accelerates. A RED block covers SGLT1; nutrient entry stops and the raster returns to baseline. Mark the plot 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Causality comes from the living mouse. Intestinal sucrose raises cervical-vagus firing. Blocking SGLT1 removes that response, placing the sugar sensor upstream.

scenes.tts: Light that silences C C K labelled gut cells abolishes the sucrose response. Light that activates the same labelled population raises vagal firing. These tests ask necessity and sufficiency.
scenes.caption: Light that silences CCK-labelled gut cells abolishes the sucrose response. Light that activates the same labelled population raises vagal firing. These tests ask necessity and sufficiency.
scenes.visual: Split the carried world vertically. Left: RED light dims the GOLD CCK-labelled cell and the BLUE firing raster flattens; label 'necessary in this test'. Right: GREEN light brightens the same population and the raster accelerates; label 'sufficient in this test'. Both halves remain marked 'mouse'.
scenes.narration: Light that silences CCK-labelled gut cells abolishes the sucrose response. Light that activates the same labelled population raises vagal firing. These tests ask necessity and sufficiency.

scenes.tts: The chain has boundaries. Cocultures are dishes. Only a minority of C C K cells contacted sensory fibres in fixed tissue. A synapse does not erase hormone signalling.
scenes.caption: The chain has boundaries. Cocultures are dishes. Only a minority of CCK cells contacted sensory fibres in fixed tissue. A synapse does not erase hormone signalling.
scenes.visual: The four-link chain stays centred. A dish outline encloses the timing and pharmacology links. Several GOLD cells appear; only a minority extend contacts to BLUE fibres. The GREY hormone dots resume diffusing beside the TEAL synapse. A boundary frame labelled 'mouse evidence' surrounds everything.
scenes.narration: The chain has boundaries. Cocultures are dishes. Only a minority of CCK cells contacted sensory fibres in fixed tissue. A synapse does not erase hormone signalling.

scenes.tts: Anatomy found the contact. Physiology identified rapid glutamate transmission. Acute manipulations connected the sensor to vagal firing. The next question is what this signal changes.
scenes.visual: The four chain segments unfold into a left-to-right route: GOLD gut sensor, TEAL synapse, BLUE vagus, then an empty outlined choice box. Activity pulses travel along the first three objects and stop at the question-marked box.
scenes.narration: Anatomy found the contact. Physiology identified rapid glutamate transmission. Acute manipulations connected the sensor to vagal firing. The next question is what this signal changes.

scenes.visual: End card over the dim carried gut world. Large centred line: 'A fast gut synapse requires a chain of evidence.' The four chain segments orbit slowly behind the text.
